reviews.comment: One of the nicest professors I've ever had! Really awful midterm, 48 average, but he doesn't want people to do poorly. He gave us an extra essay at the end of the semester for up to 15 bonus points and asked how he could make the exam better for people.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're taking 231, you'll get an A just for a basic understanding of Excel & research. He shows how to conduct every step of the projects he assigns, & the topics are pretty basic to write about. His lectures can sound very intimidating because of how knowledgeable he is on pols, but when you actually get down the the work, its' not that hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is my third class with Dr. Li and I enjoyed it. The only issue is the group project but the grading wasn't super harsh - I just got stuck with a bad partner. I would recommend this class to anyone that enjoys writing research papers or hates tests. 3 research papers (with R) and one partnered presentation. He takes attendance so go to class
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The one exam for this class is brutal and that's what brought my grade to the B. You have to attend every class and be prepared for a lot of reading and writing. We use R for our research papers so I would recommend taking Pols 209 before this class. Prof. Li is a good lecturer and gives great feedback on the in class presentations.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Quan Li is passionate, kind, caring, and genuinely learns everyone's names. This is my third class with him, but it's the easiest yet. If you have taken 209 & 309, then the R-based essay projects are a breeze. The one group project we had was a little tedious, but other than the 3 projects + group, there's no other work for this class. go register!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy but bad professor. The course description didn't match what was being taught. Only one exam but very detailed and hard, and not enough time given to finish. Class average was a 48 and no curve or retake. Long presentations and not enough time to prepare.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor himself is knowledgeable in this field and his lectures are good. For me personally, I just read the textbook he assigned us and I was completely fine for the weekly quizzes. He does struggle with using online technology. This course was 40% of textbook activities, 20% quizzes, 20% on project 1, and 20% on project 2 or take the final.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor is clearly knowledgeable about all thing's political science, from talking to others, if you don't show up to class you struggle a lot more. He shows you step by step what to do for the projects, answers emails and questions fast, and is willing to help students succeed by negotiating. He is not tech savvy, but he is an amazing professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Loved this class! Lectures can seem long but he's incredibly knowledgeable in the field. The class was very clear, he just isn't very tech savvy. He let us change due dates and was responsive to class needs. Those who only attended on quiz days (Thursdays) were always the ones confused as attendance tripled on those days. Don't skip you'll be fine.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was one of the most disorganized classes I ever. Half the time it seems he doesn't what he is talking about. For the projects, the directions are so unclear and he delayed showing us how to process the data. He also said he would be very lenient on the project grading, while his TA proceeded to take off points for the smallest reasons

Doesn't make syllabus/grading organized AT ALL. Didn't know my grade the entire semester bc he grades late & would put RANDOM grades. Isn't tech savvy- constantly mess up quiz submissions, uploading multiple, confusing students on what to complete. Research paper was confusing & had coding (isn't a coding class- was difficult for many students).
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This was one of the most difficult classes I've ever had. Not because of the material alone, but with the added fact that the functionality of the syllabus and classes made no sense, and put MANY students lower where they thought they'd be. We have weekly quizzes over material we went over a week prior. The lectures do not help whatsoever. Read.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall a great professor! He really cares about his student, so if you are ever struggling just ask for help!
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: 309 is a tough course, however Dr. Li was ALWAYS accessible and willing to help master a topic. The class is beneficial academically, but my main take away from the class was the value of investing in resources. If you are willing to put in the effort, the class is manageable. Utilizing the book and meeting with Dr. Li is the BEST way to succeed.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: When I took the class, our final grade consisted of four things; two group projects, a hard af essay test (30% of final grade), and attendance. With that being said, attendance was like 20% of the grade and the projects were very open-ended (25% of final grade each). Attend class, get a study group for the test, and an A is easily obtainable.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was one of the most challenging classes I've ever taken, and it was worth it. Prof Li's main goal is that every student walks away from his class with a greater understanding of the political economy. He goes above and beyond if you come to his office hours to make sure you're not struggling. He gives extra credit frequently and follows advice
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Worst Prof I have ever had. Yes, he is probably a genius and is very passionate about Polimetrics, but he does not care how his students do. Half the class was graduating seniors who needed this class to pass and his response to complaints on the difficulty of the material and work was: "Switch majors". Arrogant, mean, and targets students in class
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Had Dr. LI for Research Seminar POLS 483. Hands down most difficult and frustrating class ever taken. He will scare you and push you to your absolute academic limits Have much more respect for Political Scientists now that the process is clearer. ONLY take if you are willing to put 3x the amount of energy into what you have done in other classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Take him. He tells you straight up it's a hard class. Don't be scared because he is very helpful if you talk to him. I bombed the first test but it was my fault and thankfully he had 10 extra credit points because he listens to students. The presentations help you greatly although he is very honest about what you did wrong. Also weekly readings.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Li will warn you of the course's difficulty. Take him serious because the course will be difficult and involve hours of reading. I recommend forming study groups early on and working ahead. Professor Li keeps emotions and bias out, and is genuinely interested in you learning. Be kind and talk with the man, he may even offer extra credit.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He's tough, but I didn't come here to skate by.  I also found him to be quite hilarious!  If you are doing a Reasearch Seminar with him, it is VERY helpful to have had POLS309 first, or at least a VERY good 209 Professor.  I'm not ready to publish yet, but after this course, I certainly feel I could put together a solid Journal Article.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very tough class. Get ready to do A LOT of quantitative data research. You get to research the topic of your choice, but there's a lot of quantitative data and papers involved, and using R program, not STATA, and you can't miss at all or you'll be so lost. You're basically getting a taste of grad school. Very good professor overall, though.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.  Only 1 test and it is 45% of the grade.  Didn't have a grade until 3-5 days before the Q-Drop deadline.  Attendance is part of the grade.  Article readings to do for each class, but he structures the curriculum very poorly.  Nice guy, but horrible professor.  Most certainly avoid this class if you can.
